articles.title: Celtic fans throw tennis balls at club owner Dermot Desmond during golf tournament
articles.summary: Desmond escorted off St Andrews course by security. Celtic say the protest ‘brought shame upon the club’ Celtic’s principal shareholder Dermot Desmond had tennis balls thrown towards him during his visit to the Alfred Dunhill Links golf tournament at St Andrews in a protest from fans.
body: The 76-year-old – who has been criticised by supporters for an apparent lack of progress on the pitch – was taking part in the pro-am event on Saturday when the disruption happened on the green of the 15th hole.
Tennis balls with pictures of Desmond’s face crossed out were thrown on to the green, with Desmond then escorted off the course by security.
The Celtic Fans Collective later released a statement on X, which included video and pictures of the protest, calling for change at the top of the club.

“Dermot Desmond has essentially been allowed to run Celtic Football Club whilst using his wealth to hide from supporters and accountability,” the statement said. “Fans took the chance today to send a message that this arrangement cannot continue.”

articles.title: Lamine Yamal stars again as Spain see off Czechia and maintain perfect start
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal says he feels like Superman or Spider-Man sometimes, and Spain’s fans are starting to wonder if he just might be. There is something comic book hero about what the teenager is doing right now, some unexplained super power swelling inside him.
body: And yet in a game which seemed to have been done at half-time, when Spain led 2-0 after Rodrigo Hernandez had added the second and Lamine Yamal was withdrawn, his show seemingly over, the danger returned. Czechia, vastly improved after the break, pulled one back through Jiri Slama on 69 and then were denied a 79th-minute equaliser when Vassilis Fotias, the referee, who rescued Spain, harshly ruled out a Ryan Naderi goal – apparently for a foul on Robin Le Normand as the free-kick that led to it was swung in.

Reduced to 10 men soon after, still furious, Czechia finally fell with two minutes left when Mikel Merino made Spain safe. The seleccion’s first visit to the Carlos Tartiere in 11 years had ended the way they had hoped. Welcomed back as world and European champions once more, they were applauded off as winners again. A night that had begun with Rodri being presented with the World Cup by Santi Cazorla and Juan Mata, academy products at Real Oviedo and members of the generation to which all others would forever be compared, ended with a jeopardy no one anticipated when it started in a way that has become implausibly, absurdly familiar.

articles.title: Humphries to face Price in World Grand Prix final
articles.summary: World number two Luke Humphries clinched his spot in the final of the World Grand Prix with a 5-3 victory over James Wade where he will face Gerwyn Price after his 5-2 win over Nathan Aspinall.
body: World number two Luke Humphries secured his place in the World Grand Prix final with a 5-3 victory over James Wade.
Humphries averaged 96.92 and threw 10 180s as he reached the final for the fourth successive time.
The 31-year-old Englishman will face Welshman Gerwyn Price on Sunday evening in Leicester after he beat Nathan Aspinall in the other semi-final.

"I've got to do it again because there's so many major finals I've let slip. Gezzy [Price] is playing well but if I play like that again, it's going to be a cracking game and I hope it is," Humphries told Sky Sports.

articles.title: Bowie gets Pocognoli off mark with Scotland victory in North Macedonia
articles.summary: This was an occasion on which Scotland dare not stumble. By the time Kieron Bowie smashed home a seventh minute opener against a North Macedonia side not without its troubles to seek, it was already clear they would not. Bowie afforded Sébastien Pocognoli his first goal as the Scotland manager.
body: John McGinn’s 22nd goal for his country, coming from the penalty spot, meant the scoreline at least almost reflected Scotland’s dominance. Only Scott McKenna’s late sending off and a failure to notch three, four or five could have irked Pocognoli. Scotland remain alive and kicking in section B1 of the Nations League while aware they will face far, far stiffer challenges. Scotland needed to be professional in North Macedonia and met that task appropriately.

On the occasion of Andy Robertson’s 100th cap, it appeared in the early stages that the Tottenham full-back had been stung by criticism of recent performances in Scotland colours. Robertson marauded forward at will, including inside five minutes where he forced Stole Dimitrievski into a fine save. McGinn, like Robertson, has been the subject of some scathing words. McGinn’s response was as forceful as his teammate.

articles.title: Wakefield dominate Warrington in Grand Final to claim fairytale Super League title
articles.summary: Grand Final: Warrington 10-23 Wakefield. Trinity are champions for first time since 1968. Do not let anyone tell you fairytales do not exist. This is not just a maiden Super League title, or indeed a first major trophy for almost 60 years.
body: Matt Ellis promised things would change. When he took ownership of his beloved Wakefield Trinity in 2023, he inherited a club on its knees. Just relegated to the Championship, with a stadium that resembled a building site and a squad of players nobody wanted a piece of. But he insisted that within five years, Wakefield would win their first major trophy since 1968 with his investment.

In the end, he lied: it took him only three. As Wakefield lifted rugby league’s most prestigious prize aloft inside Old Trafford on Saturday evening, surely not even Ellis could have foreseen how quickly all this could have happened. It is not an exaggeration to suggest Trinity have long been seen as one of Super League’s laughing stocks; now, they are the club everyone has to catch.

Most of their recent history has been dominated by financial problems, and, year after year, simply surviving was seen as an achievement. That is not an indictment on those who came before Ellis, with the previous custodian of Wakefield, Michael Carter, playing just as key a role in this moment. Without him, this night would not have become a reality.

articles.title: Whittaker survives late scare to hold on for points win
articles.summary: British light-heavyweight Ben Whittaker survives a dramatic late onslaught from Conor Wallace to move a step closer to a world-title shot with a points victory in Birmingham.
body: The 29-year-old controlled much of the contest with his trademark showboating and superior boxing skill at the Utilita Arena before Wallace came roaring back in the championship rounds.
The Northern Irishman rocked Whittaker in the 10th and came close to a remarkable turnaround in the 12th, with the home fighter forced to hold on until the final bell.
The judges scored it 117-111, 116-112 and 115-113 as Whittaker became mandatory challenger for the IBF world title.
"It was too easy and I took my eye off the ball a little bit. He caught me with a good shot but that's boxing," Whittaker said.

articles.title: SB Nation Reacts Results: Vikings’ Biggest Offensive Problem Is Behind Center
articles.summary: We’ve got the results of our SB Nation Reacts poll for this week, and since we said we’d get them to you before kickoff on Sunday...well, it looks like we’d better get them to you now. So, let’s get to it without any further ado.
body: We’ll start the way we always start, with our question about whether or not our readers feel that our Minnesota Vikings are moving in the right direction. After a season-high following an ugly win in Week 2, a second consecutive ugly win had our fans feeling quite the opposite way after the Week 3 win over Tampa Bay.

After seeing the confidence number leap to 75% going into Week 3, it’s now plummeted to just 41% of fans believing the purple are heading in the right direction going into Week 4. Following yet another abysmal showing from the offense, it isn’t terribly difficult to understand why. Yes, it’s fun to watch Brian Flores’ defense continue to put the other team’s offense in a blender every week, but Minnesota’s offense seems to be in a constant state of disarray. Even when they put up 39 points in Week 1, they did so with the benefit of a lot of short fields and miscues from Green Bay rather than a big offensive performance, so things haven’t exactly been encouraging on that side of the ball.

articles.title: Celtic condemn fan protest as Desmond targeted at Alfred Dunhill
articles.summary: Celtic's largest shareholder Dermot Desmond is targeted in a protest at the Alfred Dunhill Links golf tournament in St Andrews as tennis balls were thrown towards him.
body: Celtic say they will "indefinitely ban" anyone "established to be involved in planning, facilitating or participating" in a protest against the club's largest shareholder Dermot Desmond at the Alfred Dunhill Links golf tournament in St Andrews.

Tennis balls with pictures of the 76-year-old's face scored out were thrown on to the green of the 15th hole of the pro-am competition, with images showing Desmond later having to be escorted off the course by security.
The statement from the club "condemns in the strongest terms" the incident, which is said was "discussed and planned in advance".

"This was a premeditated action," it added. "Accordingly, the club will no longer recognise the Celtic Fans Collective as a representative body speaking on behalf of Celtic supporters and will cease all engagement with the Collective."

body: The Rams announced that they were sacking second-year defensive coordinator Tyson Summers. The transaction appears to have been at least partially influenced by Summer's exit partway through the team's defeat.
Here's what we know about Summer's shock decision to walk out of Canvas Stadium in Collins, Colorado.

articles.title: Humphries to face Price in World Grand Prix final in 2023 repeat
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price and Luke Humphries will look for their second World Grand Prix titles when they meet in Sunday's final of the double-start event in Leicester.
body: Price, the 2020 champion, beat Nathan Aspinall 5-2 in Saturday's first semi-final before 2023 winner Luke Humphries defeated James Wade 5-3 to reach his fourth straight final and set up a repeat of the showpiece game three years ago - when he saw off Price 5-2.

A major drought will end either way at the Mattioli Arena, with Humphries going over a year since his last premier title - the 2025 Premier League - and Price's previous elite silverware coming way back in 2022 at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.
Price romped into a 3-0 lead over Aspinall, peeling off two 13-darters and then a 15-darter to sweep the opener before he broke The Asp in the deciding leg of set two.
The third set went on throw until the fourth leg, when Aspinall missed six darts to hold, including two at double one, and Price subsequently pinned D10 to move 3-0 up.

articles.title: Third time lucky for Pocognoli as Scotland mark Robertson's 100th cap with win
articles.summary: Sebastien Pocognoli secured his first Scotland win at the third time of asking as captain Andy Robertson became just the second player to reach 100 caps.
body: The head coach insisted there was no extra pressure after drawing a blank in their opening two Nations League games, but he and the players silenced some critics with a strong performance in Skopje despite a second red card inside a week as they beat North Macedonia 2-0.

Robertson missed two brilliant chances before Kieron Bowie - hooked after Jack Hendry's early sending off against Switzerland in midweek - smashed the ball into the bottom corner to earn his first international goal and Scotland's first in over 420 minutes.
Play was stopped by a dog running onto the pitch before Scotland continued to dominate with Bowie, Robertson and Ben Gannon-Doak going close before the break.
Scotland were awarded a penalty when Gannon-Doak went down in the box after half-time, only for the referee to overturn his decision after being called to the monitor.

articles.title: Scouts Unsure How To Fix Drake Maye: 'He Looks Like A Rookie, And Not A Particularly Good One'
articles.summary: Many people around the league expressed concern for Drake Maye and J.J. McCarthy following the recent struggles for the former and the trade involving the latter.
body: A year ago, the quarterbacks in the 2024 NFL Draft were all the rage. Drake Maye led the New England Patriots to the Super Bowl and was the MVP runner-up. Caleb Williams also helped the Chicago Bears win a division title, and Jayden Daniels was a year removed from a surprise NFC Championship Game appearance with the Washington Commanders.

Now, not even a month into Year 3 for the six quarterbacks taken in the first round of the 2024 draft, some cracks have emerged. Williams and Daniels have been sidelined due to injuries, while Michael Penix Jr. just returned from an ACL tear.

The bigger focus this past week, though, was on Maye and J.J. McCarthy. Maye has arguably been the worst starting quarterback in the NFL through the first three weeks of the season, with the Patriots getting out to an 0-2 start. The Minnesota Vikings, meanwhile, ripped the band-aid off the McCarthy experiment and traded him to the New York Giants for a fifth-round pick.

Why is Maye performing so badly, and are his problems fixable? What should we make of the Giants' trade for McCarthy? We asked those questions to people around the league, and many expressed concern for both quarterbacks.
